body:
The Federal Reserve held its target federal funds interest rate in the 3.50%-3.75% range at its July meeting, a decision investors generally expected. Nine members voted to leave the rate unchanged, while three members dissented, favoring a 0.25% hike. Ahead of the decision, investors expected a 35% chance of a rate increase. Elevated inflation, primarily stemming from higher energy prices, increased investor expectations for higher policy rates later this year.    The U.S. Federal Reserve (Fed) kept its policy interest rate at a range of 3.50%-3.75% citing somewhat tighter financial conditions through higher market-based rates.

   Kevin Warsh made no change to the previous, shortened Fed statement in his second meeting as Fed Chair, and reiterated the Fed’s 2% inflation target and the importance of restoring Fed credibility after years above that target.

The Federal Reserve held its target range at 3.50% to 3.75% this Wednesday, July 29th, 2026, where it has remained since December, in a 9-3 vote. A hold was the market’s base case, but it was not fully priced, as rate futures assigned roughly a one-in-three probability to a hike before the meeting, with those odds moving alongside oil prices through July.
